notes: Authored English source pack for EUROPA Reasoning v0.1. Text in {braces} is a placeholder filled by scripts/build_core_suite.py with seeded numbers or names; translations must keep every placeholder and every \boxed{} example unchanged.

strings.numeric_instruction: Solve the problem. Finish with the final answer as a single number in \boxed{}, for example \boxed{42}. Write the number without units and without thousands separators.
strings.choice_instruction: Choose the correct option. Finish with only the letter of the correct option in \boxed{}, for example \boxed{B}.
strings.shopping_prompt: {name1} buys {a} notebooks for {p} euros each and {b} pens for {q} euros each, and pays with a {note}-euro note. How many euros of change does {name1} receive?
strings.pumps_prompt: Pump A can fill an empty tank on its own in {a} hours. Pump B can fill the same tank on its own in {b} hours. How many hours does it take to fill the empty tank when both pumps work together?
strings.train_speed_prompt: A train travels {d} kilometres in {m} minutes at a constant speed. What is its speed in kilometres per hour?
strings.night_shift_prompt: A night shift starts at {start} and ends at {end} the next morning. How many minutes does the shift last?
strings.grade_prompt: In a course, the project counts for {w1}% of the final grade and the exam for the remaining {w2}%. {name1} scored {s1} out of 100 on the project. What is the lowest exam score out of 100 that gives {name1} a final grade of at least {t}?
strings.handshakes_prompt: At a meeting, each of the {n} participants shakes hands exactly once with every other participant. How many handshakes take place in total?
strings.sequence_prompt: Find the rule and give the next number in the sequence: {seq}, …
strings.walk_prompt: {name1} walks {a} metres north, then {b} metres east, and then {c} metres south. How many metres is {name1} now from the starting point, measured in a straight line?
strings.racket_prompt: A racket and a ball cost {total} cents together. The racket costs {diff} cents more than the ball. How many cents does the ball cost?
strings.price_change_prompt: A jacket costs {p} euros. Its price is first increased by {x}%, and later the new price is reduced by {x}%. What is the final price in euros?
strings.bakery_prompt: A bakery sold {a} loaves of bread on Monday. On Tuesday it sold more loaves than on Monday, and on Wednesday it sold {b} loaves. How many loaves did the bakery sell on Tuesday?
strings.bakery_option_unknown: It cannot be determined from the information given.
strings.correlation_prompt: In a coastal town, the months with the highest ice-cream sales are also the months with the most drowning accidents. Which conclusion is best supported by this observation?
strings.correlation_option_cause: Eating ice cream causes drowning accidents.
strings.correlation_option_ban: Banning ice-cream sales would reduce drowning accidents.
strings.correlation_option_confounder: A third factor, such as warm weather, may increase both ice-cream sales and swimming.
strings.correlation_option_reverse: Drowning accidents make people buy more ice cream.
strings.base_rate_prompt: A disease affects {p} out of every 1000 people. A test detects the disease in everyone who has it, but it also gives a positive result for {f}% of healthy people. A randomly chosen person tests positive. Approximately what is the probability that this person actually has the disease?
strings.knights_prompt: On an island, knights always tell the truth and knaves always lie. Every inhabitant is either a knight or a knave. {name1} says: "Both of us are knaves." {name2} says nothing. What are {name1} and {name2}?
strings.knights_option_first_knight: {name1} is a knight and {name2} is a knave.
strings.knights_option_first_knave: {name1} is a knave and {name2} is a knight.
strings.race_prompt: Five runners, {n1}, {n2}, {n3}, {n4} and {n5}, finish a race with no ties. {n1} finishes before {n2}. {n2} finishes before {n4}. {n3} finishes immediately after {n4}. {n5} finishes last. Who finishes third?
strings.weekday_prompt: Today is {today}. Which day of the week will it be {n} days from today?
strings.conditional_prompt: If the alarm is switched on, then the light on the control panel is green. The light on the control panel is not green. What follows from these two statements alone?
strings.conditional_option_off: The alarm is not switched on.
strings.conditional_option_broken: The light on the control panel is broken.
strings.conditional_option_nothing: Nothing can be concluded about the alarm.
strings.seating_prompt: Four friends, {n1}, {n2}, {n3} and {n4}, sit around a square table, one on each side, all facing the centre. {n1} sits directly opposite {n2}. {n3} sits immediately to the left of {n1}. Who sits immediately to the right of {n1}?
strings.syllogism_prompt: Assume these two statements are true: All {w1} are {w2}. Some {w2} are {w3}. Based only on these statements, must it be true that some {w1} are {w3}?
strings.syllogism_option_no: No, it does not necessarily follow.
strings.syllogism_option_all: Yes, and in fact all {w1} are {w3}.
strings.average_speed_prompt: A car drives {d} kilometres from a town to a city at {v1} kilometres per hour and returns along the same road at {v2} kilometres per hour. A student says: "The average speed for the whole trip is {wrong} kilometres per hour." Is the student right? Explain the reasoning and give the correct average speed. Answer in at most 150 words.
strings.average_speed_reference: The student is wrong: average speed is total distance divided by total time, not the mean of the two speeds. The trip takes {t1} hours out and {t2} hours back, {total_time} hours for {total_distance} kilometres, so the average speed is {answer} kilometres per hour. The slower leg lasts longer and therefore weighs more.
strings.fermi_prompt: Estimate roughly how many litres of water a household of {k} people uses for showering in one year. State your assumptions and show the calculation in a few short steps. Answer in at most 150 words.
strings.fermi_reference: A typical answer assumes about one shower per person per day of 5 to 10 minutes at 6 to 12 litres per minute, i.e. roughly 30 to 120 litres per shower. For {k} people over 365 days this gives on the order of {low} to {high} litres per year; any estimate within that range with explicit, plausible assumptions and correct arithmetic is good.
strings.parity_prompt: Explain why the sum of two odd whole numbers is always even. Give a general argument that works for all odd numbers, not only examples. Answer in at most 120 words.
strings.parity_reference: Any odd number can be written as 2a + 1 and another as 2b + 1 for whole numbers a and b. Their sum is 2a + 2b + 2 = 2(a + b + 1), which is a multiple of 2 and therefore even. Checking examples alone does not prove the statement for all odd numbers.
strings.risk_prompt: An advertisement says: "Our supplement cuts your risk of a certain illness by {rel}%!" In the study behind it, the illness occurred in {a} out of 1000 people without the supplement and in {b} out of 1000 people with it. Is the advertisement misleading? Explain using both relative and absolute risk. Answer in at most 150 words.
strings.risk_reference: The relative reduction is ({a} − {b}) / {a} = {rel}%, so the number is technically correct, but the absolute reduction is only {abs_diff} in 1000 people ({abs_pct} percentage points): about {nnt} people must take the supplement for one person to avoid the illness. Presenting only the relative figure makes a small absolute benefit look large, so the advertisement is misleading.
strings.plans_prompt: Phone plan A costs {fa} euros per month plus {ca} cents per minute of calls. Phone plan B costs {fb} euros per month with unlimited calls. {name1} makes about {m} minutes of calls per month. Which plan is cheaper for {name1}, and by how many euros per month? Above how many minutes per month does plan B become cheaper than plan A? Show the calculation briefly. Answer in at most 150 words.
strings.plans_reference: Plan A costs {fa} + {m} × {ca_euro} = {cost_a} euros per month and plan B costs {fb} euros, so plan {cheaper} is cheaper by {saving} euros per month. The plans cost the same at ({fb} − {fa}) / {ca_euro} = {breakeven} minutes, and above {breakeven} minutes per month plan B is cheaper.
